prompt: What is the maximum pulling tension on one 4/0 AWG copper conductor (211,600 cmil) using 0.008 lb/cmil?
correct: About 1,693 lb, unless the pulling device limit is lower (the lowest limit wins)
options: About 1,693 lb, unless the pulling device limit is lower (the lowest limit wins)
explanation: 211,600 x 0.008 = 1,693 lb. Compare with the pulling eye (manufacturer rating or 10,000 lb) and basket grip (about 1,000 lb) and use the lowest.
quote: All Copper Soft 0.008

prompt: In ladder or ventilated tray, what is the fill rule for multiconductor cables 4/0 AWG and larger?
correct: A single layer, with the sum of the cable diameters no more than the tray width
options: A single layer, with the sum of the cable diameters no more than the tray width
Up to 40% of the tray area, stacked any way
No limit, because tray is not a raceway
explanation: Smaller cables are limited by cross-sectional area from NEC Table 392.22(A).
quote: Cables 4/0 AWG and larger: The sum of the cable diameters can't exceed the tray width, and the cables must lie in a single layer.

prompt: What does NEC 110.14(D) require when terminating conductors?
correct: A calibrated torque tool (approved means) when the manufacturer gives a torque value
options: A calibrated torque tool (approved means) when the manufacturer gives a torque value
Re-torquing every connection after one week
explanation: Loose terminations heat up, oxidize and can arc; record the torque and mark the connection.
quote: requires the use of a torque tool to terminate conductors when a numerical value is provided by the equipment manufacturer

prompt: A megger test reads 1.5 megohms and the spec requires 100 megohms. What do you do?
correct: Fail it: record it, report it, and do not energize
options: Fail it: record it, report it, and do not energize
Pass it, because any reading above zero is fine
Retest at a lower voltage until it passes
Energize it and watch for trouble
explanation: The project spec sets the pass value; a reading below it is a failed test that goes on the NCR / test log.

prompt: What must be done before any insulation resistance (megger) test?
correct: De-energize, lock out, verify zero energy, and disconnect electronics
options: De-energize, lock out, verify zero energy, and disconnect electronics
Nothing: the megger is safe on live circuits
Energize the circuit to warm the insulation
Remove all labels from the cable
explanation: Never connect a megger to energized lines or equipment, and discharge the cable afterwards.
quote: Never connect a Megger insulation tester to energized lines or equipment.

prompt: Before a power cable pull, what should the cable itself be checked for?
correct: Correct size and type, shipping damage, end seals, special instructions
options: Correct size and type, shipping damage, end seals, special instructions
Nothing: it was checked at the factory
explanation: The small details decide whether damaged cable has to be pulled back out.
quote: Check cable for: a. Correct size and type b. Shipping damage c. End seals d. Special instructions

prompt: What should the cable reel be checked for before a pull?
correct: Damage, protruding nails that might damage the cable, and staples
options: Damage, protruding nails that might damage the cable, and staples
explanation: A nail or staple in the flange can cut the jacket as the cable pays off.
quote: Check reels for: a. Damage b. Protruding nails that might damage cable c. Staples

prompt: How must a forklift lift a cable reel?
correct: By contacting both flanges
explanation: Lifting on the cable crushes it; a crane needs a shaft through the arbor hole or a cradle under both flanges.
quote: Forklifts must lift the reel by contacting both flanges.

prompt: Where should cable reels be stored?
correct: On a hard surface, so the flanges cannot sink and let the reel weight rest on the cable
options: On a hard surface, so the flanges cannot sink and let the reel weight rest on the cable
Lying flat on their side in mud
Stacked on top of each other
explanation: Store reels out of harm's way as well.
quote: Store reels on hard surface so that the flanges will not sink and allow reel weight to rest on cable.

prompt: Cable is to be installed in cold weather. What does Southwire recommend?
correct: Keep it in heated storage for at least 24 hours before installation and pull more slowly
options: Keep it in heated storage for at least 24 hours before installation and pull more slowly
Pull it faster before it gets colder
Heat it with a torch on the reel
Cold makes no difference to cable
explanation: Each insulation or jacket type also has a minimum installation temperature.
quote: they should be kept in heated storage for at least 24 hours before installation

prompt: Which of these is required of a cable pulling lubricant?
correct: UL or CSA listed, compatible with the cable, and containing no waxes or greases
options: UL or CSA listed, compatible with the cable, and containing no waxes or greases
Motor oil, because it is slippery
None: power cable is always pulled dry
explanation: The lubricant and its residue must not harm the cable or propagate flame.
quote: The lubricant should contain no waxes or greases.

prompt: What is the tension limit for a pulling eye?
correct: The eye manufacturer's rating or 10,000 lb, whichever is less
options: The eye manufacturer's rating or 10,000 lb, whichever is less
Unlimited, if the winch can do it
explanation: The allowable pull is the lowest of the conductor, device and sidewall-pressure limits.
quote: Do not exceed the allowable tension stated by the manufacturer of the pulling eye or 10,000 pounds, whichever is less.

prompt: Traditional conservative practice limits the tension on a basket grip to ____.
explanation: A basket grip holds the jacket, so it is limited well below a pulling eye.
quote: Traditional conservative practices limit the allowable tension of a basket grip to 1,000 pounds.

prompt: Which factor is the most restrictive in many power cable pulls?
correct: Sidewall pressure at the bends
options: The length of the pull rope
explanation: Sidewall pressure is the force on the cable as it is pulled around a bend.
quote: Excessive sidewall pressure can cause cable damage and is the most restrictive factor in many installations.

prompt: How can sidewall pressure on a cable pulled around a bend in tray be reduced?
correct: Use a larger-radius sheave
explanation: Sheave radius must meet both the minimum bend radius and the sidewall pressure limit.
quote: Sidewall pressure can be reduced by using a large radius sheave.

prompt: Minimum bending radius for Type TC tray cable 1.0 inch or less in diameter (NEC 336.24)?
correct: 4 x the cable diameter
explanation: TC: 4 x up to 1 in, 5 x for 1 to 2 in, 6 x above 2 in; 12 x with metallic shielding.
quote: a) Diameter 1.0 inch or less 4 b) Diameter between 1.0 inch to 2.0 inches 5 c) Diameter larger than 2.0 inches 6

prompt: Why must power cable ends always be sealed?
correct: To keep moisture out
options: To make the cable easier to pull
To show the cable has been tested
explanation: Check end seals on receipt and keep them sealed until termination.
quote: Cable ends must always be sealed to prevent the entrance of moisture

prompt: Under NEC Article 392, what is a cable tray?
correct: A support system for cables, not a raceway
options: A support system for cables, not a raceway
explanation: Cables in tray must be wiring methods allowed in tray on their own (for example Type TC or MC).
quote: A cable tray is a support system for cables.

prompt: Control and signal cable only, in a solid bottom tray. What is the fill limit?
correct: 40% of the tray's inside cross-sectional area
options: 40% of the tray's inside cross-sectional area
explanation: 50% in ladder or ventilated tray, 40% in solid bottom tray.
quote: Fill is limited to 50 percent of the tray's inside cross-sectional area in ladder or ventilated tray, and 40 percent in solid bottom tray.

prompt: Can medium-voltage and 480 V power cables share the same tray?
correct: Only with a solid fixed barrier between them, or if the MV cables are Type MC
options: Only with a solid fixed barrier between them, or if the MV cables are Type MC
Yes, if they are different colours
quote: NEC 392.20 doesn't allow that unless there's a solid fixed barrier

prompt: What does NEC 392.60 require of metal cable tray that supports electrical conductors?
correct: It is bonded and grounded, and the tray system is electrically continuous
options: It is bonded and grounded, and the tray system is electrically continuous
It must be insulated from ground
explanation: At splices, expansion joints and gaps, continuity comes from approved connections or bonding jumpers.
quote: Metal cable tray that supports electrical conductors has to be bonded and grounded like any other conductor enclosure, and the tray system has to be electrically continuous.

prompt: Besides fill, what else can limit how much cable a tray may carry?
correct: Its load rating and support span
options: Its load rating and support span
explanation: A heavily loaded tray on a long span can reach its weight limit before its fill limit (NEMA VE 1).
quote: a heavily loaded tray on a long support span can hit its weight limit before it hits its fill limit

prompt: What happens over time at a termination that was not torqued properly?
correct: Resistance increases and the connection heats up
options: Resistance increases and the connection heats up
Nothing, if it passed the first test
explanation: Heat degrades the termination and insulation; oxidation and arcing can follow.
quote: Loose connections due to improper torqueing lead to increased resistance over time at the termination causing a temperature rise at the connection.

prompt: Should terminations be re-torqued after the initial proper torque was applied?
correct: No, it is not recommended; use infrared scans and visual inspection instead
options: No, it is not recommended; use infrared scans and visual inspection instead
Only by hand without a tool
explanation: If absolutely necessary, a tool set to 90% of the value may check for looseness, on a de-energized circuit.
quote: It is not recommended to "re-torque" terminations after the initial application of the proper torque during installation.

prompt: How do inspectors commonly verify that terminations were torqued correctly?
correct: Check torque tools and their calibration certificates, observe connections, and get the installer's certification
options: Check torque tools and their calibration certificates, observe connections, and get the installer's certification
Ask the crew if they remember
Pull on each conductor by hand
explanation: Photos and videos are also becoming common for remote verification.
quote: site verification of torque tools and calibration certificates

prompt: What rule of thumb does Megger give for minimum insulation resistance?
correct: About 1 megohm per 1,000 V of operating voltage, with a minimum of 1 megohm
options: About 1 megohm per 1,000 V of operating voltage, with a minimum of 1 megohm
explanation: The project spec or NETA tables set the actual acceptance value.
quote: Insulation resistance should be approximately one megohm for each 1,000 volts of operating voltage, with a minimum value of one megohm.

prompt: What is the polarization index in insulation testing?
correct: The 10-minute reading divided by the 1-minute reading
options: The 10-minute reading divided by the 1-minute reading
The test voltage divided by the current
The cable length times the reading
explanation: A ratio below 1 indicates dangerous insulation; above 4 excellent (Megger's table).
quote: If the ratio is a 10-minute reading divided by a 1-minute reading, the value is called the polarization index.

prompt: After an insulation resistance test, how long should the test leads stay connected?
correct: At least 30 to 60 seconds, to let the capacitance discharge
options: At least 30 to 60 seconds, to let the capacitance discharge
explanation: A cable stores charge from the test voltage.
quote: Do not disconnect the test leads for at least 30 to 60 seconds following a test, allowing time for capacitance discharge.

prompt: Why should insulation resistance readings be compared at about the same temperature?
correct: Insulation resistance drops as temperature (and moisture) rises
options: Insulation resistance drops as temperature (and moisture) rises
The megger only works at 20 C
explanation: Make tests at about the same temperature or correct them to the same temperature.
quote: Also you should make tests at about the same temperature, or correct them to the same temperature.

prompt: Which DC test voltages are commonly used for routine insulation tests on 440 to 550 V equipment?
explanation: A 600 V cable is typically tested at 1,000 V DC; the spec sets the voltage and pass value.
quote: 440 to 550 volts 500 and 1,000 volts

prompt: Under Southwire's '2 to 50 megohm rule' for evaluating insulation resistance readings, which reading is considered acceptable?
correct: 50 megohms or higher
explanation: Readings between 2 and 50 megohms call for investigation; always apply the project spec.
quote: A megohm meter reading of 50 megohms or higher should be considered acceptable.

prompt: While one phase of a cable is under insulation test, what happens to the other phases?
correct: They remain grounded at all ends
options: They remain grounded at all ends
explanation: Remove grounds only from the phase being tested.
quote: Phases not under test are to remain grounded at all ends.

prompt: Which instrument can be used for a simple conductor continuity check end to end?
correct: An ohmmeter or a megohm meter
options: An ohmmeter or a megohm meter
explanation: Check each conductor end to end and record the result per conductor.
quote: A continuity test can be accomplished with an ohmmeter or megohm meter tester.
